originalAlarm.description: Value stored to 'wakeup' is never read

reasoning: FALSE POSITIVE: The alarm fires on 'wakeup = 0' at line 6 (inside #ifndef CONFIG_BF60x) when CONFIG_BF60x is false. In the simplified file, wakeup is set to 0 but the function returns 0 immediately without using it. In the real Linux kernel bfin_pm_suspend_mem_enter(), wakeup is used as a return value or in conditional logic after this assignment — the simplification dropped those uses. This is a simplification artifact. The known vbdb bug is an UnusedVariable when CONFIG_BF60x is *enabled* (wakeup declared but never assigned because the assignment is inside #ifndef BF60x) — the opposite configuration.
